leave_behind.text: A React JSX child that is a plain object THROWS ('Objects are not valid as a React child'), it does not implicitly stringify to '[object Object]' the way template-literal or string-concatenation interpolation of the same value would. When a dispatch describes an object reaching customer-visible copy as producing literal '[object Object]' text, verify which specific JS operation actually touches the value (JSX child vs. template literal vs. string concat) before assuming the described failure mode is the real one -- in this case the real failure was a harder one (a render crash), not a softer garbled-text one, even though the underlying 'customer-facing break' claim was correct.

This codebase's own established test seam for exactly this class of defect already exists: components with a disclosure/accordion pattern export the disclosure component directly with `isOpen` as a driven prop specifically so renderToStaticMarkup (which never runs effects/click handlers) can test the EXPANDED state without touching internal useState. Look for that seam ('Exported test seam' in the docstring) before assuming a stateful component's hidden content is untestable.
